v.why: In conv-heavy cells a 0->3 residual path helps (+0.2 to +16 pp), while in pool- or skip-dominated cells it is strongly harmful (down to -40 pp).
Filling an empty 2->3 edge with a 3x3 conv adds a new computational path, a larger gain than swapping out an existing op (runs 1 vs 2-4, 5 vs 6-8, 74 vs 75).
In weak 1x1/pool cells, adding a 3x3 conv on 2->3 gives large gains (+2 to +17 pp), versus small or negative gains in cells already full of 3x3 convs.
When edge 5 is already empty, removing edge 4 leaves only the 0->3 path into the output, costing 6-15 pp versus about 0-2.5 pp otherwise.
Turning an empty 1->3 edge into a conv restores a path to the output, which helps more than replacing a skip connection (63/65 vs 64/66).
Without the 0->3 shortcut, deepening edge 0 to a 3x3 conv hurts optimization, especially on ImageNet16 (-4 to -13 pp vs about +1.5 pp with the shortcut).
A conv on 0->2 is only useful when node 2 feeds the output; with edge 5 as a skip it gives large gains (85, 87, 38), but little or nothing when edge 5 is none.
Adding a conv where the 0->3 edge was empty adds an output path (+2 to +12 pp), whereas replacing a skip connection with a conv removes the residual and hurts.
When edge 4 carries a conv, node 1 feeds the output directly, so cutting its input edge 0 costs more (32/34 vs 31/33, 82/84 vs 81/83).
If node 2 does not reach the output, the op on edge 2 barely matters, so swapping its conv for a skip is near-neutral rather than harmful (68/70 vs 67/69).
